decisions.reason: The source decision's effect on SQ11 is already fully represented by the existing message-77 MODIFY to shot_specification_method.
The source decision's effect on SQ4 is already fully represented by the existing message-77 MODIFY to storyboard_mismatch_specification_method.

The existing message-77 Event records the preferred reference format but leaves the broader storyboard-mismatch specification stating that every mismatch will be handled only through a detailed description. That attribute must also reflect the optional example frames and updated-reel alternative.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Because I’m not good at updating the storyboard reel yet and doing so takes me too long, I’d prefer to try more detailed shot descriptions, possibly supported by example frames I find online. Updating the reel myself remains an option as well.

value_updates.storyboard_mismatch_specification: For parts that differ from the storyboard reel, use detailed shot descriptions, optionally supported by online example frames; an updated storyboard reel remains an alternative.
value_updates.preferred_shot_direction_reference_forma: Use detailed shot descriptions, optionally supported by online example frames; an updated storyboard reel remains an alternative.

decisions.reason: The source changes how shot directions and storyboard mismatches are communicated, not the SQ4 energy-blast behavior or its lifecycle.
Changing the preferred shot-specification format does not alter the existing image-quality rules, including script precedence and permission to generate improved set images.
The shot-specification method has no effect on the requirement that the final video be in full color.
The source does not change the final video's vertical 9:16 format.
The source changes the medium used to communicate shot directions but does not change the established character-pair counts or framing progression.
Optional example frames for shot descriptions do not change the requirement that new sets remain stylistically consistent across shots.
The source does not alter the required visual distinctness among revised sets.
The general shot-description method does not change the content or deferred status of the opening aerial establishing shot.
The source does not change which bridges must be removed or retained in the Kestrel images.
